newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper calls for unity to fight rebels.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper calls for unity to fight rebels.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper sidestepped Colombian lawmakers' demands to adopt crisis measures and on Wednesday called on them to close ranks around the government to confront the growing leftist rebel threat.

Samper spoke in the wake of calls from ruling Liberal Party senators for him to shut down Congress and assume emergency powers to quell the escalating violence from illegal armed groups of the left and right that have pledged to disrupt upcoming local elections.
Others legislators said Samper should step down and face impeachment for his inability to guarantee law and order.

"What the subversives are trying to achieve with their campaign of pre-election terrorism is to divide political leaders," Samper told reporters after a meeting of his security council. "They want to set us against one another to disturb the electoral climate and discredit the path of democracy."

Contrary to expectations, neither Samper nor Defense Minister Gilberto Echeverri declared a 90-day emergency -- known as a "state of internal commotion" -- which would have enabled the government to decree special laws to combat the guerrillas.

During Tuesday night's congressional committee debate, Sen. Julio Cesar Guerra, a Samper loyalist, said, "We offer to (allow the president to) close Congress ... to make war or peace. We must do everything in our power to get peace in Colombia."
But Sen. Juan Guillermo Angel, also a Liberal, said Samper should be impeached because he had "lost his authority."

In the last month, scores of civilians, mostly peasants, have been massacred by guerrillas and right-wing death squads across the country. At least five mayors were kidnapped by rebels in the southern province of Narino and released on Tuesday night after more than a week in captivity.

But the attack that most shocked the political establishment was the killing of Liberal Party Sen. Jorge Cristo, one of Samper's most loyal allies, by rebels of the National Liberation Army (ELN) in northeast Colombia Friday.
The rise in violence, despite Samper's calls for new peace talks with the country's Marxist guerrilla armies, comes ahead of elections for provincial governors and mayors in October.
Right-wing paramilitary groups and leftist guerrillas have threatened to kill candidates opposed to their own views.
